[…] The Devils Lake Basin is an endorheic, or closed, basin covering about 9,800 square kilometers in northeastern North Dakota.}} # {{senseid|en|any insect of family Muscidae, nontechnical usage}} {{lb|en|non-technical}} Especially, any of the insects of the family {{taxfmt|Muscidae|family}}, such as the common [[housefly]] (other families of Diptera include [[mosquito]]es and [[midge]]s). #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=5|passage=When you're well enough off so's you don't have to fret about anything but your heft or your diseases you begin to get queer, I suppose. And the queerer the cure for those ailings the bigger the attraction. A place like the Right Livers' Rest was bound to draw freaks, same as molasses draws '''flies'''.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Dennis Webster|title='An indictment of South Africa': whites-only town Orania is booming|url=https://www.theguardian.com/cities/2019/oct/24/an-indictment-of-south-africa-whites-only-town-orania-is-booming|date=2019-10-24|passage=October in Orania can be charming. When the sun sets, long ribbons of burnt orange settle on the horizon. The '''flies''' and mosquitoes that come with the oppressive summer heat haven’t arrived yet. It is Magdalene Kleynhans’ favourite time of year. “You can sit outside until late into the night,” says the businesswoman, whose family spend much of their time outdoors. Her children fish from the banks of the Orange River whenever they choose. Kleynhans leaves the house unlocked. “It’s a good life. It’s a big privilege.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329100257/https://www.theguardian.com/cities/2019/oct/24/an-indictment-of-south-africa-whites-only-town-orania-is-booming}} # {{senseid|en|any flying insect, nontechnical usage}} Those or any similar but not closely related insect, such as a [[dragonfly]], [[butterfly]], or [[gallfly]]. # {{senseid|en|fishing}} {{lb|en|fishing}} A lightweight fishing [[lure]] [[resemble|resembling]] an insect. # {{senseid|en|chest exercise}} {{lb|en|weightlifting}} A [[chest]] [[exercise]] performed by moving extended [[arm]]s from the sides to in front of the [[chest]]. More at [[flee]] and [[flow]]. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|flew|flown}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[travel]] through the [[air]], another [[gas]]{{,}} or a [[vacuum]], without being in contact with a grounded surface. #: {{syn|en|ascend|aviate||float|[[flutter]] (birds)|glide|hover|rise|skim|soar|wing}} #: {{cot|en|walk|swim}} #: {{ux|en|Birds of passage '''fly''' to warmer regions as it gets colder in winter.}} #: {{ux|en|The probe '''flew''' beyond the solar system.}} #: {{ux|en|The Concorde '''flew''' from Paris to New York faster than any other passenger airplane.}} #: {{ux|en|It takes about eleven hours to '''fly''' from Frankfurt to Hong Kong.}} #: {{ux|en|The little fairy '''flew''' home on the back of her friend, the giant eagle.}} #* {{RQ:Chesterton Orthodoxy|passage=Angels can '''fly''' because they take themselves lightly.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1972|artist={{w|Black Sabbath}}|title={{w|Supernaut (song)|Supernaut}}|passage=I want to reach out and touch the sky / I want to touch the sun, but I don't need to '''fly'''}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-09-07|volume=408|issue=8852|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21584962-small-remote-controlled-craft-powered-sun-are-taking-air On a bright new wing]| passage='''Flying''' using only the power of the sun is an enticing prospect. But manned solar-powered aircraft are fragile and slow, […].}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To take a [[flight]] on a [[plane]]; to [[pilot]] or [[crew]] a [[plane]]. ##: {{ux|en|My airline needs me to get clearance before I can '''fly''' again.}} ##: {{ux|en|If we want to '''fly''' today, we need to leave for the airport right now.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|entomology|of [[moth]]s or [[butterfly|butterflies]]}} To be in the [[winged]] [[adult]] [[stage]]. ##: {{ux|en|This species '''flies''' from late summer until frost.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|colloquial|figurative|of a [[proposal]], [[project]] or [[idea]]}} To be [[accepted]], [[come about]] or [[work out]]. ##: {{ux|en|Let's see if that idea '''flies'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|You know, I just don't think that's going to '''fly'''. Why don't you spend your time on something better?}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause to fly {{gloss|travel or float in the air}}: to [[transport]] via air or the like. #: {{ux|en|Charles Lindbergh '''flew''' his airplane The Spirit of St. Louis across the Atlantic ocean.}} #: {{ux|en|Birds '''fly''' their prey to their nest to feed it to their young.}} #: {{ux|en|Each day the postal service '''flies''' thousands of letters around the globe.}} #* {{RQ:Gilbert and Sullivan Pirates of Penzance|passage=The brave black flag I '''fly'''.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-09-07| volume=408| issue=8852| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21584962-small-remote-controlled-craft-powered-sun-are-taking-air On a bright new wing]| passage=A solar-powered unmanned aerial system (a UAS, more commonly called a drone) could '''fly''' long, lonely missions that conventional aircraft would not be capable of.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[arrange]] for someone to take a flight. ##: {{ux|en|We '''flew''' the kids out to see their grandparents.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[pilot]] a plane over a region or on a route. ##: {{ux|en|This is the first time I '''flew''' the Pacific.}} ##: {{ux|en|I'm hoping to '''fly''' the London-New York route so I can see the Big Apple again.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To complete (a goal, task, mission, etc.) while [[crew#Verb|crewing]] an aircraft or spacecraft. ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[hunt]] with a [[hawk]]. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1590|author={{w|Robert Greene (dramatist)|Robert Greene}}|title=w:Friar Bacon and Friar Bungay|passage=We'll '''fly''' the partridge, or go rouse the deer.}} # {{lb|en|ergative}} To wave or flutter; to cause to wave or flutter. #: {{ux|en|When the wind picked up, her hair '''flew''' back behind her head.}} #: {{ux|en|In her dance, she holds her hands above her head to '''fly''' those colorful ribbons in the air.}} ## {{lb|en|ergative}} To operate a [[kite]] ''(A lightweight toy or other device... carried on the wind and tethered and controlled from the ground by one or more lines)''. ##: {{ux|en|Why don’t you go outside and '''fly''' kites, kids? The wind is just perfect.}} ## {{lb|en|ergative}} To display (a flag) on a flagpole; to be displayed on a flagpole. ##: {{ux|en|We '''flew''' the state flag under the national flag.}} ##: {{ux|en|The flag '''flew''' at half-mast.}} ##: {{ux|en|The American flag '''flies''' in every state and territory.}} ### {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To proudly and openly make one's allegiances or viewpoint apparent. ###: {{ux|en|She's really letting the freak flag '''fly'''.}} ###: {{ux|en|Only one candidate is willing to '''fly''' the conservative flag boldly.}} ### {{lb|en|ergative|figurative}} To symbolically rule over or control. ###: {{ux|en|The French flag '''flew''' over Louisiana until 1803.}} ###: {{ux|en|The king endeavored to '''fly''' his nation's flag over new territories.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To drain away or be expended quickly. #: {{ux|en|The family fortune '''flew''' in a few short years.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|dated}} To [[vanish]]; to [[fade away]]. ##: {{syn|en|dissipate}} ##: {{ux|en|The mist '''flew''' by noon.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively}} To [[travel]] or [[proceed]] very fast; to [[hasten]]. #: {{syn|en|dart|flit|speed|see also [[Thesaurus:move quickly]]}} #: {{ux|en|He '''flew''' down the hill on his bicycle.}} #: {{ux|en|It's five o'clock already. Doesn't time '''fly'''?}} #* '''1870''', {{w|William Cullen Bryant}} (translator), ''The Iliad'' (originally by {{w|Homer}}) ## {{lb|en|intransitive|figuratively}} To [[move]] [[suddenly]], or with [[violence]]; to [[carry out]] an [[act]] [[suddenly]] or [[swiftly]]. ##: {{syn|en|hurry|zoom|see also [[Thesaurus:rush]]}} ##: {{ant|en|see also: [[Thesaurus:move slowly]]}} ##: {{ux|en|a door '''flies''' open}} ##: {{ux|en|a bomb '''flies''' apart}} ##* {{RQ:Dickens Haunted House|chapter=The Mortals in the House|page=7|column=1|passage=And in respect of the great necessity there is, my darling, for more employments being within the reach of Woman than our civilisation has as yet assigned to her, don’t '''fly''' at the unfortunate men, even those men who are at first sight in your way, as if they were the natural oppressors of your sex {{...}}}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1976|author=J. P. Reading|chapter=15|title=Tanya|location=New York, N.Y.|publisher=[[w:Scholastic Corporation|Scholastic Book Services]]|page=174|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/tanya0000jpre/page/174/mode/1up|oclc=5034286|passage=I was upstairs, trying hastily to fix my face and unredden my eyes when I heard a car on the drive and '''flew''' to a window to make sure that it was David.}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive|figurative}} To [[proceed]] with [[great]] [[success]]. ##: {{ux|en|His career is really '''flying''' at the moment.}} ##: {{ux|en|One moment the company was '''flying''' high, the next it was on its knees.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|archaic|literary}} To [[avoid]] or [[shun]]. ##: {{ux|en|I must '''fly''' the temptation of drink.}} ## {{lb|en|ambitransitive|archaic|poetic}} To [[flee]], to [[escape]] (from). ##: {{syn|en|abscond|escape|flee|see also [[Thesaurus:flee]]}} ##: {{ant|en|remain|stay}} ##: {{ux|en|My bird '''flew''' the cage.}} ##: {{ux|en|'''Fly''', my lord! The enemy are upon us!}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|act=IV|scene=iv|page=56|column=1|passage=[V]pon a [[sudden|ſodaine]], / As ''[[w:Falstaff|Falſtaffe]]'', ſhe, and I, are newly met, / Let them [children dressed like "urchins, [[ouphe]]s and fairies"] from forth a ſaw-pit ruſh at once / With ſome diffuſed ſong: Vpon their ſight / We two, in great amazedneſſe will '''flye''': {{...}}}} ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|act=3|scene=ii|passage=to '''fly''' the favours of so good a king}} ##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=5|passage='''Fly''', ere evil intercept thy flight.|year=1873}} ##* {{RQ:Dryden Juvenal Satires|14|passage=Sleep '''flies''' the wretch.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1829|author=w:Edgar Allan Poe|chapter={{w|Tamerlane (poem)|Tamerlane}}|title=Al Aaraaf, Tamerlane and Minor Poems|passage=And boyhood is a summer sun
Whose waning is the dreariest one —
For all we live to know is known
And all we seek to keep hath '''flown''' — {{...}}}} ##* {{RQ:Tolkien Fellowship of the Ring|passage=He staggered and fell, grasped vainly at the stone, and slid into the abyss. “'''Fly''', you
